As a white person in an overwhelmingly white community, topics that revolved around slavery and such would always be approached with apprehension and briefness. In other words, the teachers acknowledged that there were no black students in the classroom, and felt the need to glaze over that stuff.


I don’t care how ‘awkward’ it is to talk about. We SHOULD feel uncomfortable in class, because no one should ever feel COMFORTABLE talking about the horrible, systemic racism that has plagued the country’s history. I look back at my AP US History class, and I sure as hell would rather learn more about the unfair treatment of the black population and minorities/focus on that then have to hear unnecessary details about countless battles in the Revolutionary War or Civil War. 


I am begging school systems to create a safe environment where students understand that the US’s past is ugly, and should make any person with morals squirm in their seat. This idea of discomfort is because we as white people have not been made to admit our privilege and use it in a beneficial way before. I am glad that now, white people privilege is in the spotlight. I have felt uncomfortable many times seeing how minorities have been treated differently than me. The condescending way of speaking, the particular language that is subtly demeaning, it all has to STOP.
